events.title: Drone strikes ignite fires at Ryazan and Novokuibyshevsk refineries
events.detail: Ukrainian drones struck the Ryazan refinery (one of Moscow's main fuel arteries) and the Novokuibyshevsk refinery in Samara region on the morning of August 2, 2025, igniting large fires. This strike is widely marked as the opening blow of the sustained refinery campaign that triggered the crisis.

events.title: Crimea and Russia's Far East report first gasoline shortages
events.detail: Crimea and Russia's far east became the first territories to experience visible gasoline shortages in August 2025, as refining capacity losses from the opening wave of strikes began to bite in regions farthest from alternate supply routes.

events.title: Ryazan refinery struck again in powerful explosion
events.detail: A second major strike hit the Ryazan refinery on August 27, 2025, with a powerful explosion reported. Analyst Boris Aronstein described the emerging pattern of repeated, coordinated drone waves as "the most severe crisis in recent years," noting Russia could not repair refineries fast enough between attacks.

events.title: Krasnodar (Afipsky) and Syzran refineries hit overnight
events.detail: Ukrainian drone forces struck two more major refineries overnight on August 30 — the Krasnodar-area (Afipsky) refinery in southern Russia and the Syzran refinery in Samara region — igniting fires and explosions and widening the geographic spread of capacity losses.

events.title: Ukrainian drones strike Rosneft's Ryazan refinery again
events.detail: A further drone strike hit the Rosneft-owned Ryazan refinery, part of a sustained campaign that by autumn 2025 had produced roughly a dozen distinct strikes on the facility across the year.

events.title: Russian regions begin rationing gasoline as strikes cripple refineries
events.detail: By late September 2025, regional authorities across Russia began imposing sales restrictions on gasoline as repeated refinery strikes cut into local supply, the first widespread rationing measures of the crisis.

events.title: Fuel crisis spreads nationwide: rising prices, rationing, empty pumps
events.detail: Forbes documented the rapid nationwide spread of the crisis by September 29, 2025 — rising prices, formal rationing, long queues and pumps running dry in parts of southern and central Russia and the Volga region.

events.title: Crimea imposes 20-liter purchase cap and price caps
events.detail: Occupied Crimea introduced a 20-liter-per-customer purchase limit alongside retail price caps in October 2025. Some independent gas stations closed rather than sell at capped prices under antitrust rules preventing price increases.

events.title: Government extends gasoline export ban, suspends fuel damper mechanism
events.detail: Moscow extended its gasoline export ban through May 1, 2026, imposed a moratorium on zeroing-out the fuel damper (a subsidy mechanism), and exempted winter diesel from excise duty — an early package of policy responses aimed at holding down domestic prices.

events.title: IEA: refining capacity down 20% at peak, oil revenue lowest since 2022
events.detail: Reuters and the IEA reported that at the peak of the autumn 2025 strike wave, roughly 20% of Russian refining capacity was offline, though overall national oil processing fell only about 3–6% as unaffected refineries partially compensated. Russia's oil export revenue fell to its lowest level since the start of the 2022 invasion.

events.title: New Western sanctions loom as analysts call crisis worst since the 1990s
events.detail: The US, EU and UK signaled new sanctions that threatened to cut Russian energy revenue further in 2026. Analyst Craig Kennedy described the unfolding fuel crisis as "the worst crisis in Russia's energy sector since the 1990s."

events.title: Ninth 2025 strike on Ryazan refinery
events.detail: Drones hit the Ryazan refinery for the ninth documented time in 2025, causing another fire — underscoring the difficulty Russia faced keeping repeatedly-targeted facilities online.

events.title: Syzran oil refinery targeted in overnight drone strike
events.detail: The Rosneft-owned Syzran refinery was struck again overnight, part of the sustained pattern of repeat attacks that kept significant national capacity offline heading into 2026.

events.title: Wholesale gasoline prices jump on renewed refinery strikes
events.detail: Russian wholesale gasoline prices rose sharply in mid-February 2026 as another round of drone strikes on refineries tightened domestic supply, an early signal that the crisis had not eased over the winter.

events.title: Satellite imagery detects fires at Ust-Luga multimodal complex
events.detail: NASA fire-detection satellite data recorded blazes at the Ust-Luga Multimodal Complex on the Baltic coast on March 26, 2026, part of the widening target set of Ukraine's deep-strike campaign against Russian energy export infrastructure.

events.title: Russia cuts 2026 growth forecast on oil revenue and wartime pressure
events.detail: The government downgraded its 2026 economic growth forecast, citing weaker oil revenues, elevated inflation and the compounding strain of wartime spending — with the fuel crisis cited as an accelerating factor.

era: National Emergency: Omsk, Saratov & the Diesel Ban (Jun–Jul 2026)

events.title: Russia Day strikes hit Taneco and Taif-NK refineries in Nizhnekamsk
events.detail: Ukraine launched long-range drone strikes on June 12, 2026 (Russia Day) against the Taneco and Taif-NK refineries in Nizhnekamsk, Tatarstan — one of the deepest strikes of the campaign to date — plus the Togliattikauchuk chemical plant in Samara region. Taneco, owned by Tatneft and with capacity over 16 million tons/year, completely halted refining operations.

events.title: Bank of Russia flags fuel-crisis inflation risk
events.detail: The Bank of Russia publicly flagged the fuel crisis and mounting war costs as key upside risks to inflation, ahead of monthly inflation accelerating sharply in June.

events.title: Deputy PM Novak floats a "total ban" on diesel exports
events.detail: Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said the government was considering a full, producer-inclusive ban on diesel exports to redirect supply to the domestic market, a significant escalation from earlier restrictions that had exempted major oil companies.

events.title: Fuel crisis rationing spreads to 56+ regions
events.detail: The Moscow Times reported rationing measures active in more than 56 Russian regions, including Tyva (highest recorded price, 90.63 RUB/liter), Khakassia, Kursk (20-liter cap), Khanty-Mansi, Sakhalin, Tatarstan, Sverdlovsk, Sakha, Kabardino-Balkaria, Karelia and Irkutsk.

events.title: Crimea and Sevastopol declare state of emergency over fuel crisis
events.detail: Crimean head Sergei Aksyonov signed a decree declaring a state of emergency across occupied Crimea and Sevastopol effective 1:00 p.m. on June 26, 2026, amid an energy crisis and near-total suspension of fuel sales. Gasoline was largely reserved for emergency services, police, and businesses with existing supply contracts; children's admission to summer camps was suspended.

events.title: Kremlin weighs reviving Euro-2 diesel standard, banned since 2013
events.detail: Kommersant reported the Kremlin was considering reauthorizing Euro-2 diesel fuel — a lower-quality standard banned in Russia since 2013 — as an emergency measure to stretch domestic supply.

events.title: Putin publicly admits fuel shortages, calls them "not critical"
events.detail: President Putin acknowledged fuel shortages for the first time in public remarks to government ministers, saying "right now we're observing a certain shortage, but it's not critical," while confirming a full diesel export ban was under consideration. ISW assessed the remarks as an attempt to "promote a facade of stability."

events.title: Kremlin confirms rare talks to import gasoline
events.detail: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov confirmed Russia — one of the world's largest oil exporters — was in active talks to import gasoline from abroad, saying imports would proceed "if agreements can be reached at acceptable price points," while declining to name partner countries.

events.title: Gasoline imports from Belarus surge nearly 20-fold
events.detail: Russia's gasoline imports from Belarus hit a record high in June 2026, reaching roughly 141,000 tonnes in the first 25 days of the month — about 2.4 times May's volume and roughly 20 times June 2025 levels — as Minsk redirected supplies previously bound for Central Asia.

events.title: Mishustin signs Euro-3 gasoline decree as crisis hits 78 of 83 regions
events.detail: PM Mikhail Mishustin signed a decree allowing refineries to produce lower-grade Euro-3 gasoline (up to 150 mg/kg sulfur, non-exportable) instead of Euro-5 through the end of 2026. The same day, Novaya Gazeta reported the crisis had reached at least 78 of Russia's 83 regions plus occupied territories, with 38 regions imposing sales restrictions and Penza, Irkutsk and Zabaykalsky declaring states of emergency.

events.title: Deep strike halts Omsk refinery, Russia's largest
events.detail: A Ukrainian long-range drone strike — reportedly by special operations forces, 2,500 km from the front — hit the Gazprom Neft-owned Omsk refinery on July 6, 2026, striking the ELOU-AVT-11 primary distillation unit and the CDU-10 unit (38% of throughput). Omsk is Russia's largest refinery, processing about 440,000 barrels/day and normally producing ~5 million tons of gasoline and 8 million tons of diesel a year; it lost roughly three-quarters of its production capacity and halted operations the next day.

events.title: Saratov refinery struck, halts operations
events.detail: One day after the Omsk strike, drones hit the Saratov oil refinery, forcing it to halt operations and compounding the sudden loss of two major refineries in the same week.

events.title: Russia bans all diesel exports, including from producers
events.detail: At a government meeting chaired by President Putin, Deputy PM Novak announced a full ban on diesel fuel exports effective July 8, 2026 — extending the earlier restriction (which had applied only to non-producer traders) to oil companies themselves, in order to redirect supply to the domestic market.

events.title: FT: 50 million people affected, June crude throughput down 28%
events.detail: The Financial Times reported Russia processed 4.1 million barrels of crude per day in June 2026 — 28% below the five-year average and 35% below design capacity — with the fuel shortage directly affecting an estimated 50 million people, or 35% of the population. Ukraine's General Staff put disabled refining capacity at 42.74%; the IEA said "more than 20%"; Finnish President Alexander Stubb estimated a 40% reduction.

events.title: Fuel crisis raises stagflation fears as growth stalls
events.detail: The Moscow Times reported the fuel crisis was compounding stagnant growth and accelerating inflation, with monthly inflation hitting a seasonally-adjusted annualized 10.6% in June (up from 2% in May), driving fresh stagflation warnings from economists.

events.title: Novak: gasoline export ban extended to year-end, diesel ban to ease gradually
events.detail: Deputy PM Novak said the gasoline export ban would be extended through the end of 2026, while diesel export restrictions would be lifted gradually "as the market recovers," without giving a firm timeline.

events.title: Government formally extends fuel export ban through January 2027
events.detail: Russia formally extended its combined gasoline and diesel export ban through January 2027. Separately, Sberbank CEO German Gref told shareholders he did not believe anyone in the country was primarily concerned with anything other than an end to military hostilities, an unusually candid remark from a senior state-bank executive.

events.title: Zelensky: Ukraine strikes Yaroslavl refinery for second night running
events.detail: President Zelensky said Ukrainian forces struck oil facilities deep inside Russia, including the large Yaroslavl Oblast refinery hit for a second consecutive night, part of what he called a campaign of "long-range sanctions" against the infrastructure funding the war.

events.title: Nizhnekamsk drone strike kills 13 in deadliest attack in two years
events.detail: A large-scale Ukrainian drone strike on industrial and civilian sites in Nizhnekamsk, Tatarstan killed at least 13 people and wounded dozens, according to regional authorities — the deadliest single strike of the deep-strike campaign in two years, again targeting the Taneco refinery complex.

events.title: Second shortage wave hits Orenburg, Lipetsk, Sochi
events.detail: A fresh wave of shortages prompted Orenburg region to cap purchases at 30 liters of gasoline / 60 liters of diesel with an odd-even license-plate refueling system (effective Aug 12), Lipetsk region to adopt a 30-liter cap with the same odd-even system (effective Aug 13), and Sochi to reinstate purchase limits, with the city administration urging residents to avoid using personal vehicles. Deputy PM Novak convened an interagency coordination meeting on Aug 11.

events.title: Ten regions retighten restrictions after brief relaxation
events.detail: Ten regions — Orenburg, Lipetsk, Tver, Krasnodar, Zabaykalsky, Primorsky, Krasnoyarsk, Oryol, Tuva and Khakassia — reimposed or tightened sales restrictions on August 14, 2026 after having relaxed them in late July, signaling the crisis had not durably eased.

events.title: Reuters: second nationwide shortage wave, gasoline sales down 20%
events.detail: Reuters reported a second nationwide wave of fuel shortages, with SPIMEX exchange data showing gasoline sales down 20% in the first half of August versus late July. Moscow Oblast reported filling stations completely out of gasoline (though diesel remained available), and six regions had adopted odd/even license-plate rationing systems.

events.title: Lower-quality Euro-3 fuel blamed for mass vehicle breakdowns
events.detail: In the first half of August 2026, reports emerged of engine failures and breakdowns in vehicles designed for higher-grade Euro-5 gasoline, attributed to the emergency Euro-3 standard authorized in July — an early sign of the policy's costs even as it helped stretch fuel supply.

events.title: Orsk refinery fully shut down, repairs could take 6 months
events.detail: Ukrainian drones struck the Orsknefteorgsintez refinery in Orsk, Orenburg region, on Aug 11, sparking a fire and completely halting operations. Orenburg Governor Yevgeny Solntsev said shrapnel damaged "key infrastructure" that cannot be quickly repaired due to Western sanctions on imported equipment, with repairs potentially taking up to six months at the medium-sized refinery (nameplate capacity ~115,200 bpd).

media.caption: Orsk refinery fire after Ukrainian drone strike, Aug 11 2026

events.title: Gazprom Neftekhim Salavat refinery struck again, fire reported
events.detail: Ukrainian drones struck the Gazprom Neftekhim Salavat oil refining complex in Bashkortostan overnight on Aug 13 — the facility's third confirmed hit since July 2026 — sparking a fire as part of a broader overnight wave that also struck a Wildberries logistics hub in the same region. The refinery accounts for roughly 2.7% of Russia's total refining throughput.

media.caption: Fire at Gazprom Neftekhim Salavat refinery after drone strike, Aug 13 2026

events.title: Greek-owned tanker and grain ship struck near Novorossiysk export terminal
events.detail: A Greek-managed Suezmax tanker (the Skiros, loaded at the Caspian Pipeline Consortium terminal) and a separate Greek-owned grain vessel were struck by drones near Novorossiysk — which handles roughly 700,000 barrels/day of Russian oil exports — extending Ukraine's deep-strike campaign to export shipping and further threatening Russia's last major Black Sea outlet.

events.title: Drone strikes hit Yaroslavl's Slavneft-YANOS refinery and Samara's Kuibyshev refinery
events.detail: Ukrainian drones struck the Slavneft-YANOS refinery in Yaroslavl overnight, killing one civilian and injuring 27 when debris hit an intercity bus, and separately damaged both crude distillation units (CDU-4, CDU-5) at Rosneft's Kuibyshev refinery in Samara, halting it again just a week after it resumed operations from a major overhaul.

media.caption: Fire at the Slavneft-YANOS oil refinery in Yaroslavl after an overnight Ukrainian drone strike, Aug 28 2026

events.title: Reuters: national gasoline output falls to ~70% of domestic demand
events.detail: Reuters reported, citing industry sources, that Russia's gasoline output fell to roughly 70% of domestic demand by late August after renewed refinery outages in Perm, Nizhny Novgorod and Yaroslavl widened the daily production-demand gap to about 35,000 tonnes, forcing greater reliance on seaborne imports from Asia (~270,000 t in August) and Belarus (~150,000 t).

events.title: Fire reported at Kirishi (KINEF) refinery, Russia's second-largest, as it prepared to resume output
events.detail: A drone strike sparked a fire overnight at the Kirishi (KINEF) oil refinery in Leningrad region — Russia's second-largest refinery by capacity and the largest in the country's northwest, with annual processing capacity of about 20 million tonnes (roughly 6% of national refining throughput). Russian air defenses said 62 drones were downed over Leningrad region; one downed drone fell near the refinery and ignited a blaze that was later extinguished, with no casualties reported. The strike — at least the sixth confirmed attack on the facility during the war — landed as KINEF was preparing to resume full operations after months of repairs from earlier March and May strikes, raising the risk of a renewed delay to restored capacity just as national gasoline output sits near 70% of domestic demand.

media.caption: Fire reported at the Kirishi (KINEF) oil refinery in Leningrad region after an overnight drone strike, Aug 30 2026

events.title: Russia expands downgraded-fuel decree to Euro-2 and Euro-4, extends it through mid-2027
events.detail: The Russian government adopted a new decree, effective Sept 1 2026, expanding the emergency fuel-quality rollback beyond the Euro-3 gasoline authorized in Mishustin's July decree to also permit production, import and sale of Euro-2 and Euro-4 grade gasoline and diesel — grades banned since 2013 — through June 30, 2027. The Energy Ministry framed the move as an anti-crisis measure to "make supplies more stable and reduce the risk of shortages." Euro-2 permits up to 50 times more sulfur than the Euro-5 standard Russia completed transitioning to in 2016; gas stations will be required to disclose the environmental class of fuel sold at the pump. The expansion follows widespread reports since early August of engine damage and breakdowns — especially in turbocharged, direct-injection engines common in Chinese-made cars — linked to the Euro-3 fuel already in circulation.

media.caption: Russia authorizes sale of Euro-2 and Euro-4 grade fuel through mid-2027 as domestic shortage drags on

events.title: Novak says fuel market 'partially stabilized' at Eastern Economic Forum, acknowledges lingering gasoline shortfall
events.detail: Speaking to reporters on the sidelines of the Eastern Economic Forum in Vladivostok, Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said Russia's domestic market is now fully supplied with diesel and jet fuel, while gasoline still faces "a shortage at the moment, but it is small." He said the situation had "improved somewhat this week" after a number of refineries resumed operations and supplied additional volumes, though minor shortages persist at filling stations in the Siberian and Ural federal districts, which he attributed to "purely a logistics issue." Novak said Russia has sufficient domestic capacity to repair 100% of its refineries and that the government will keep balancing the market through higher domestic output and additional fuel imports.

media.caption: Deputy PM Alexander Novak briefs reporters on the domestic fuel market at the Eastern Economic Forum, Sept 3 2026

events.title: Drone strike sets fire to Novorossiysk fuel oil terminal, Russia's key Black Sea export hub
events.detail: Ukrainian drones struck Russia's Novorossiysk seaport overnight on Sept 8-9, hitting the port's fuel oil terminal — a facility handling roughly 4 million tonnes a year of fuel oil and light petroleum products — and damaging at least one storage tank, OSINT monitor ASTRA reported. Novorossiysk is Russia's largest Black Sea port and a key outlet for Russian oil-product exports, as well as the terminus of the CPC pipeline carrying over 80% of Kazakhstan's crude exports. Novorossiysk Mayor Andrey Kravchenko confirmed a fire broke out, attributing it to falling drone debris; no one was injured, though debris also damaged a nearby residential building. The strike lands on a facility central to Moscow's oil-product export flows even as domestic gasoline supply remains tight.

media.caption: Fire at the Novorossiysk fuel oil terminal after a drone strike, Sept 9 2026

events.title: Saratov refinery struck a second time in a week — ELOU-AVT-6 unit and pipeline hit
events.detail: Ukraine's General Staff confirmed a second drone strike on the Saratov oil refinery overnight on Sept 11, just three days after the Sept 8 strike on the same plant. The attack reportedly damaged the ELOU-AVT-6 primary crude distillation unit and a section of the refinery's main pipeline; fires were reported on site. The facility, which processes roughly 7 million tonnes of crude annually, supplies fuel to Russian military forces as well as the civilian market. No casualties were reported.

media.caption: Fire at Saratov oil refinery after a second drone strike within a week, Sept 11 2026

events.title: Drones hit Slavyansk-on-Kuban and Nizhnekamsk (Taneco) refineries overnight
events.detail: Ukraine's General Staff confirmed strikes overnight on Sept 12-13 against the Slavyansk-ECO oil refinery in Slavyansk-on-Kuban, Krasnodar Krai (nominal capacity 5.2 million tonnes/year) and the Taneco refinery complex in Nizhnekamsk, Tatarstan, the same hub hit in the deadly Aug 10 2026 strike. NASA's FIRMS satellite service detected strong thermal radiation near the Slavyansk plant, and residents reported thick smoke over the site by dawn; Ukraine's General Staff said the refinery's key oil-processing unit and tank farm were hit. At Nizhnekamsk, a fire was reported in one of the Taneco complex's storage tanks.

media.caption: Fire at the Slavyansk-ECO oil refinery in Slavyansk-on-Kuban after an overnight drone strike, Sept 13 2026

events.title: Syzran refinery strike leaves it with no working distillation capacity; Reuters finds half of Russia's top diesel refineries curtailed
events.detail: A Ukrainian Special Operations Forces strike overnight Sept 14-15 hit the AVT-6 primary crude distillation unit at Rosneft's Syzran refinery — 71% of the plant's processing capacity — leaving the 8.9-million-tonne/year plant with no functioning distillation capacity, since its smaller CDU-5 unit was already offline from a July strike; industry sources told Reuters the refinery halted operations Sept 15, with repairs expected to take at least a month. The same overnight wave also struck the Atlant Aero drone-production facility in Taganrog. Separately, Reuters reported that three of Russia's six largest diesel refineries (roughly half of national diesel output) were now shut or running at a fraction of capacity — Kirishi fully offline since Sept 2, Volgograd and NORSI at ~25% of nameplate capacity, and Taneco's damage still being assessed — with combined diesel/gasoil exports down to about 1.8 million tonnes a month from a typical 2.5-3.4 million. The IEA said a Russian refinery has been hit on average once every three days in 2026, part of a campaign of at least 70 confirmed refinery strikes since January. Leningrad Oblast separately announced a 30-liter per-fill-up purchase cap, effective through Oct 1, after the Kirishi (KINEF) shutdown left about 20% of independent stations unable to source fuel.

media.caption: Reported Ukrainian strike on Russia's Syzran oil refinery, overnight Sept 14-15, 2026

events.title: Drone strike sparks major fire at Yaroslavl's Slavneft-YANOS refinery, one of Russia's five largest
events.detail: A Ukrainian drone attack overnight on Sept 16-17 hit the primary oil distillation unit at the Slavneft-YANOS refinery in Yaroslavl, sparking a large fire, regional governor Mikhail Yevraev confirmed. The plant — jointly controlled by Rosneft and Gazprom, with roughly 15 million tonnes/year (~300,000 bpd) of crude capacity — is among Russia's five largest refineries and has now caught fire at least nine times in 2026. No casualties were reported and the fire was fully extinguished by Thursday morning, but authorities closed a section of the M-8 federal highway linking Yaroslavl to Moscow.

media.caption: Fire at the Slavneft-YANOS refinery in Yaroslavl after an overnight drone strike, Sept 17 2026

events.title: Drones hit Moscow's own Kapotnya refinery — supplier of 40% of the capital's fuel — in year's largest overnight barrage
events.detail: Ukrainian drones struck the Gazprom Neft-owned Moscow Refinery in the capital's Kapotnya district overnight on Sept 19-20, reportedly hitting the combined oil refining unit (CORU) and the ELOU-AVT-6 primary distillation unit and sparking a large fire, Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin confirmed. The plant — one of Russia's ten largest refineries at roughly 11 million tonnes/year of capacity, just 15km from the Kremlin — supplies about 40% of Moscow city's fuel market and 70% of the wider Moscow region's petrol and aviation-gas demand. Sobyanin called it the most massive Ukrainian drone assault on the capital to date, with authorities claiming roughly 450 drones intercepted approaching Moscow and over 1,600 downed nationwide overnight; a separate hit on a logistics warehouse complex in Ramensky district and falling debris elsewhere in Moscow Oblast left at least two dead and six injured, though no casualties were reported at the refinery itself. The attack landed on the final day of Russia's parliamentary elections.

media.caption: Fire at the Moscow Refinery in Kapotnya after an overnight drone strike, Sept 20 2026

events.title: Moscow Oil Refinery confirmed fully halted after Sept 20 drone strike; repairs expected to take weeks
events.detail: Industry sources confirmed to Reuters that the Gazprom Neft-owned Moscow Oil Refinery in Kapotnya completely stopped crude processing after the overnight Sept 19-20 drone strike set fire to both of its primary units — the AVT-6 crude distillation unit (21,400 tonnes/day, 53% of total capacity) and the integrated Euro+ refining complex (18,800 tonnes/day, 47% of capacity). Repairs are expected to take several weeks. The refinery stopped offering fuel for sale on the St. Petersburg International Mercantile Exchange starting Monday, Sept 21, confirming the shutdown is total rather than partial. The plant, Russia's largest by some measures at 11.6 million tonnes/year and located just 15km from the Kremlin, normally supplies 35-40% of Moscow city's fuel and up to 70% of the wider region's petrol and aviation-kerosene demand, making its full stoppage the most consequential single outage of the crisis to date for the country's largest fuel-consumption market.

media.caption: The Moscow Oil Refinery in Kapotnya, fully halted after the Sept 20 drone strike

events.title: Drones hit Kuibyshev refinery in Samara and Bashneft-UNPZ refinery in Ufa; one killed
events.detail: Ukrainian drones struck two more Rosneft-owned refineries overnight Sept 21-22: the Kuibyshev refinery near Samara (a drone alert sounded at 3:15am, with air defense active until 4:07am before fires broke out; Militarnyi's imagery analysis suggests the AVT-5 crude unit, roughly 10,000 tonnes/day of capacity, was hit) and the Bashneft-UNPZ refinery in Ufa, Bashkortostan, about 1,300km from the Ukrainian border. Samara region Governor Vyacheslav Fedorishchev confirmed the strike on Telegram, reporting one person killed and four wounded near the Kuibyshev site; Russia's Defense Ministry said 297 drones were intercepted nationwide overnight. Kuibyshev was already left fully offline once before, after a June 10 strike hit both its AVT-4 and AVT-5 units.

media.caption: Smoke rises above the Kuibyshev refinery in Samara after an overnight drone strike, Sept 22 2026

events.title: Kaluga reintroduces odd-even rationing, Zabaikalsky caps sales at 15 liters as regions respond to renewed refinery strikes
events.detail: More Russian regions reimposed fuel purchase limits this week as the renewed drone campaign against refineries (Yaroslavl Sept 17, Moscow Sept 20, Samara/Ufa Sept 22) fed through to retail supply. Kaluga region, southwest of Moscow, brought back an odd-even system tied to vehicle license-plate numbers and banned sales into portable canisters starting Wednesday; Governor Vladislav Shapsha said 'the lines [at gas stations] are back,' calling the renewed queues understandable given the pressure on supply. In Siberia's Zabaikalsky region, authorities capped purchases of AI-92 and AI-95 gasoline at 15 liters (about 4 gallons) per vehicle across 48 stations, with local reserves of roughly 17,000 tonnes projected to last about 20 days. The moves follow Leningrad Oblast's 30-liter cap (in place since mid-September, through Oct 1) and come as the national average gasoline price reached 78.51 RUB/L in mid-September, up 21% since the start of the year, with Ukraine's military claiming more than 45% of Russian refining capacity has now been knocked offline.

media.caption: Fuel rationing spreads to Kaluga and Zabaikalsky regions amid renewed refinery strikes, Sept 23 2026
